jobs.description:
Job Description

At Nordstrom, we're more than a luxury retailer – we're a company built on a foundation of customer service, innovation, and a relentless commitment to delivering the best experiences for our customers. Technology is at the heart of our ability to create these experiences, and we're on an exciting journey to leverage AI and agents to make those moments even more personalized, seamless, and impactful.

We're looking for a collaborative and forward-thinking Director of Engineering, PDLC Agents Platform
to lead the strategy, development, and delivery of Nordstrom's agentic software delivery system — the platform that guides engineering teams from idea to shipped, production feature through named specialist digital worker agents (AI personas assigned to specific required gates in the delivery lifecycle, such as security, architecture, UX, process compliance, and SRE), persistent project memory, and enforced safety guardrails. This role sits at the center of Nordstrom's transformation towards an AI Native Operating Model for its product development lifecycle. The role owns the multi-agent platform that enables this transformation.

The platform spans the full breadth of a complex agentic system including orchestration, CLI based UI, context engineering, cost management, observability, evaluations, governance, reporting and integration with 3P coding agents (e.g. Claude Code) and models. You'll work closely with stakeholders across not just the central AI organization but all engineering teams across Nordstrom as well as all business and technical context owners for various domains. This is a highly technical leadership role where you'll build technology and cultivate a culture of engineering rigor, safe experimentation, and continuous learning. Experience with building agentic systems involving evaluations and context engineering is a requirement.

This role is offered as hybrid in Seattle, WA. Candidates must be available to work in office at the Nordstrom corporate headquarters a minimum of 4 days/week to be considered for this position.

A day in the life...

Set the Vision: Define the strategy and roadmap for the PDLC Agents Platform, aligned to Nordstrom's AI-Native Operating Model and broader business and technology goals.
Build the Paved Road: Lead development of the platform's digital worker (agent) fleet and the delivery lifecycle it enforces — project initialization, product design, development, ship and operate — so the compliant path is the fastest path.
Make Shipping a Real Gate: Own the platform's ship-time policy gate so no agent or change ships unless it's registered, instrumented, guardrail-wrapped, and eval-backed.
Collaborate Across Teams: Partner with Security, UX, Architecture, Data Science, Product, and the run-time control-plane team to define and enforce one policy-as-code spine — data classification (including PCI/PII boundaries), approved tools and models, and autonomy tiers — consistently at build time and run time.
Lead with Standards: Drive adoption of open agent standards — MCP (Model Context Protocol), A2A (Agent-to-Agent), and OTEL GenAI tracing — as the platform's framework-agnostic foundation, so authoring stays open rather than locked to one vendor.
Grow the Team: Build, mentor, and inspire a high-performing engineering team, and build a succession and talent pipeline of engineering managers and senior engineers.
Drive Operational Excellence: Establish best practices for the end-to-end agent lifecycle — build, ship, monitor, and retire — with an emphasis on scalability, security, and responsible autonomy.
Partner on Rollout: Work with domain engineering and business leaders (Merchandising, Customer Experience, and other pilot domains) to roll out AI-Native squads, confirm required guardrails run every cycle, and support teams as they progress up the autonomy "autopilot dial."

You own this if you have...

10+ years of software engineering experience, with at least 5 years in leadership roles, including experience leading platform, developer-tools, or agentic/AI engineering teams.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (advanced degrees are a plus).
Have a strong technical background in agentic AI systems in production — coding agents, multi-agent orchestration, context engineering and agentic evaluations.
Understand build-time versus run-time governance trade-offs, and have designed or enforced policy-as-code controls in a regulated or high-stakes environment.
Are a natural collaborator and communicator, able to translate complex technical concepts for a variety of audiences and build strong partnerships across Security, Data Science, and Product.
Have a proven track record of hiring, mentoring, and growing engineering teams, with an ability to inspire and motivate others through a major platform migration.
Are passionate about using AI and agents to solve meaningful problems and create exceptional, trustworthy customer experiences.

We'd Love It If You Also…

Have working knowledge of agent standards and run-time governance tooling: MCP, A2A, OTEL GenAI, agent identity/on-behalf-of ("OBO") authorization, and AI gateway or observability platforms.
Have experience in retail, e-commerce, or other customer-focused industries with PCI (Payment Card Industry) or PII (Personally Identifiable Information) data-handling requirements.

NO AGENCIES / NO SPONSORSHIP

Position Summary

The Engineering Director provides strategic and hands-on technical leadership across all engineering functions at Ladish Valves. This role owns the full lifecycle of valve design and development — from initial customer specification through prototype fabrication, performance testing, regulatory compliance, and production release. The Engineering Director serves as the company's foremost technical authority on valve design, materials science, alloy selection, surface finishing, and precision lapping, ensuring that every product shipped meets or exceeds customer performance requirements and industry standards.
This is a high-visibility leadership position that partners closely with Sales, Manufacturing, Quality Assurance, and executive management to translate complex customer requirements into manufacturable, competitive valve solutions.
Valve Design & Engineering

Lead the end-to-end design of industrial valves including gate, globe, ball, check, butterfly, and specialty valves across pressure classes ANSI 150 through 4500.
Develop and maintain design standards, engineering calculations, and tolerance specifications for all valve families.
Direct the use of CAD/CAE tools (SolidWorks, AutoCAD, FEA) to produce detailed 3-D models, assembly drawings, and manufacturing packages.
Establish and enforce design-for-manufacturability (DFM) and design-for-testability (DFT) principles throughout the engineering team.
Oversee engineering change management, ensuring all design revisions are controlled, documented, and communicated to affected departments.
Research and integrate emerging design methodologies, seal technologies, and actuation systems to keep Ladish Valves at the competitive forefront.

Customization & Application Engineering

Act as the primary technical interface with customers requiring non-standard or highly engineered valve configurations.
Translate customer P&IDs, datasheets, purchase specifications, and operational parameters into fully engineered valve designs.
Provide detailed technical proposals, engineering data books, and application analyses in support of Sales during the quote and contract phase.
Lead technical review meetings (TQMs, kick-off meetings, and ITP reviews) with customers, third-party inspection agencies, and end users.
Manage engineering deliverables on engineered-to-order (ETO) and major project contracts, ensuring schedule and technical compliance.

Testing, Qualification & Performance Validation

Own the design, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the Ladish Valves test lab, including hydrostatic, pneumatic, cryogenic, fugitive emission, and functional test equipment.
Establish and enforce valve testing procedures in accordance with API 598, API 6D, , ASME B16.34, and customer-specific test specifications.
Direct root-cause analysis and corrective action for field failures, test rejections, and non-conformances, driving permanent engineering solutions.
Develop and maintain a valve qualification and type-test library to accelerate customer approval processes.
Establish performance benchmarking programs to compare Ladish Valves products against competitive offerings.

Materials, Alloys & Metallurgy

Direct alloy and material selection for all valve pressure-containing components, trim, fasteners, and seals, considering process compatibility, temperature, pressure, corrosion, and erosion requirements.
Interpret and apply NACE MR0175/ISO 15156 and MR0103 requirements for service applications.
Partner with third-party metallurgical labs for failure analysis, material certifications, and special testing as needed (PWHT, impact testing, PMI).
Maintain Ladish Valves' approved material and supplier list; qualify new material sources in accordance with applicable codes and customer requirements.

Standards, Codes & Regulatory Compliance

Ensure all valve designs comply with applicable standards including ASME B16.34, API 600, API 602, API 608, API 6D, , and customer-specific specifications.
Maintain awareness of updates to industry codes and proactively assess impact on existing and future product lines.
Support product certifications including CE/PED (2014/68/EU), EAC, ATEX, SIL, and fugitive-emission certifications (ISO 15848, TA-Luft).

Team Leadership & Development

Lead, mentor, and develop a team of mechanical engineers, design engineers, application engineers, and drafters.
Set performance objectives, conduct regular reviews, and foster a culture of technical excellence and continuous improvement.
Manage engineering workload, project prioritization, and resource allocation across concurrent programs.
Champion cross-functional collaboration between Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, and Sales.
Drive the implementation of engineering best practices, PLM/PDM systems, and document control processes.

Education

Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, or closely related discipline from an ABET-accredited program. (Master’s degree preferred.)

Experience

Minimum 12 years of progressive engineering experience in the industrial valve or rotating equipment industry.
Minimum 5 years in an engineering leadership or management role.
Demonstrated hands-on experience with multiple valve types (gate, globe, ball, check, butterfly, needle, and/or specialty valves).
Direct experience with valve testing protocols (API 598, ISO 5208, API 6D, or equivalent).
Proven track record of designing and delivering custom engineered valve solutions for oil & gas, petrochemical, power generation, or chemical process industries.
Extensive knowledge of multiple alloy systems including carbon steel, stainless steel, duplex stainless, and nickel-based alloys.
Hands-on background with precision lapping, seating surface finishing, or related machining processes strongly preferred.

Technical Skills

Proficiency in SolidWorks; experience with FEA simulation software
Strong working knowledge of ASME B16.34, API 600/602/608/6D/, MSS SP standards, and NACE MR0175/MR0103.
Ability to read and interpret complex P&IDs, valve datasheets, and customer purchase specifications.

Exceptional ability to communicate complex technical information to non-technical stakeholders, customers, and executive management.

Professional Engineer (PE) license.

Familiarity with SIL assessment and functional safety standards (IEC 61508/61511).
Background with additive manufacturing or advanced manufacturing technologies for valve components.
Experience managing multi-site or global engineering teams.

Regular work performed in an office and manufacturing/machine shop environment.

Occasional lifting of valve components and test equipment up to 50 lbs.
Exposure to manufacturing noise, machine oils, and metal particulates consistent with a valve manufacturing facility; PPE required in production areas.

Director, Enterprise AI Platform Engineering

BMO is building a dedicated AI Engineering function to deliver the platform capabilities that make enterprise AI safe, governed, and scalable across our business domains and regulatory regimes. We are seeking an experienced technical leader to own the core infrastructure that governs and enforces how AI runs at BMO
- the AI Gateway, Policy Engine, Identity Fabric, AI Registry, Guardrails Runtime, and AI Observability.

This is a build-and-run
leadership role. You will lead a team that designs, ships, and operates the control and orchestration infrastructure sitting between policy authoring and inline enforcement — the capabilities every AI workload at BMO consumes to be secure, compliant, and observable. You will not own the AI models or applications themselves (those are domain-owned); you own the governed platform they run on
, and the runtime evidence that proves they run within policy.

You are a hands-on technical leader who has built platform capabilities at scale, operates what you build, and designs for operability and regulatory defensibility from day one. You blend deep engineering credibility with the executive presence to partner across Security, Architecture, DevOps, and domain teams. You are energized by taking real engineering assets — an existing developer portal, AI registry, a body of policy-as-code, and gateway integrations — and formalizing, scaling, and governing them into an enterprise-grade platform.

What You'll Own

Enterprise Control Plane

Developer Portal & AI Registry - productionize the developer portal; deliver a federated AI Registry spanning agents, models, tools, channels, and evaluations, with self-service onboarding and lifecycle workflows.
Policy Engine - policy-as-code infrastructure (Cedar/OPA), a policy compilation and GitOps distribution pipeline, risk-tiered approval workflows, and a policy simulation environment.
Observability & Audit - a multi-pipeline architecture spanning operational, security, and compliance telemetry; OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions; cross-pipeline trace correlation; and a tamper-evident audit lake producing regulator-ready evidence.
Governance & Lifecycle - certification workflows, automated compliance scoring, decommission governance, and evidence generation for architecture and model-risk review.

Domain Orchestration

Gateway Runtime - domain-hub deployment across multiple clouds; an inline enforcement engine with request-time policy evaluation, routing, residency, budget/quota controls, and circuit breakers, operating within strict latency budgets.
Guardrails Runtime - a multi-stage safety pipeline (input moderation, prompt-injection defense, PII handling, output validation, hallucination detection, policy enforcement) with bilingual (EN/FR) parity and behavioral guardrails for agentic workloads.
Identity Fabric - workload identity for AI (SPIFFE/SPIRE), token-exchange bridging, per-domain trust boundaries, enterprise identity integration, and cross-cloud token federation with zero-trust attestation.

What You'll Deliver (First 12 Months)

A production-hardened Developer Portal and federated AI Registry with sub-5-day self-service onboarding.
An AI Gateway operational in a selected business domain, meeting tiered latency targets.
Policy-as-code infrastructure distributing domain-scoped policy bundles via GitOps, with a working simulation sandbox.
A runtime evidence pipeline producing lineage-stamped, audit-ready traces aligned to model-risk and regulatory expectations.
A team scaled from an initial core (8–12 FTE) toward steady-state through a blend of net-new hiring and reallocation of experienced internal engineers.

How You'll Work

Build-run integrated - your team operates what it builds; there is no separate run team. You design for operability and Engineering support from the start.
Federated - you own the enforcement infrastructure domains consume; domains own their workloads. You enable, you don't centralize execution.
Evidence-first - regulatory evidence (e.g., OSFI E-23, OCC model-risk expectations) is produced at runtime through instrumented infrastructure, not assembled retroactively.
Capability-aligned - your teams own outcomes ("Identity Fabric works across all platforms"), not specific technologies.

Required Core Skills

Organizational & People Leadership

8+ years in technical platform, infrastructure, or AI/ML engineering roles in a large enterprise, including 4+ years leading and managing engineering teams.
Proven organizational leadership: building and scaling engineering teams from a small core to steady-state, including workforce planning, hiring, succession planning, and structuring squads for clear ownership and accountability.
Demonstrated team building across blended teams — integrating net-new hires with reallocated and seconded internal engineers into a single high-performing team with shared identity and standards.
Strong mentoring and coaching track record: developing engineers and technical leads, growing depth and bench strength, giving effective performance feedback, and creating clear technical growth pathways.
Ability to establish and sustain a healthy, inclusive team culture that promotes psychological safety, mutual respect, recognition, and employee engagement, aligned to BMO Values.
Experience leading through change and ambiguity — standing up a new function, aligning a team to a fast-evolving mandate, and maintaining momentum under tight timelines.
Conflict resolution and cross-team influence, including partnering with peer Directors on shared roadmaps and resolving competing priorities.

Platform & AI Engineering Depth

Demonstrated experience building and operating platform capabilities at scale — API gateways, policy/authorization systems, identity/workload-identity infrastructure, observability pipelines, or equivalent shared services.
Strong knowledge of GenAI platform engineering: LLM/AI gateways, model routing and abstraction, RAG and agentic patterns, guardrails, and AI evaluation approaches.
Hands-on experience with policy-as-code and authorization systems (Cedar, OPA/Rego, or equivalent) and GitOps-based distribution.
Experience with workload identity and zero-trust patterns (SPIFFE/SPIRE, mTLS, token exchange, federated identity) — or strong adjacent identity/security engineering depth.
Strong observability engineering background: OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, and telemetry pipelines across operational, security, and compliance domains.
Multi-cloud fluency (AWS and Azure preferred), cloud-native architecture, containerization/Kubernetes, and Infrastructure as Code.
Hands-on familiarity with modern AI/ML tooling (e.g., Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, SageMaker, Databricks, MLflow, LangChain, or equivalents) sufficient to lead technical direction.
Proven CI/CD, DevSecOps, and MLOps/LLMOps delivery experience.

Governance, Strategy & Communication

Solid grounding in Responsible AI, AI/data governance, privacy, and — ideally — model-risk management and financial-services regulatory expectations.
Executive-grade communication and relationship management across technical and senior-leadership audiences (written, verbal, and presentation).
Strategic and organizational management skills, including multi-year roadmap planning, budgeting, forecasting, and vendor engagement in partnership with Vendor Management.
A critical thinker with strong analytical, problem-solving, and prioritization abilities across a complex, multi-stakeholder portfolio.

Education & Certifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline (Master's preferred).
Relevant certifications an asset: cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) architecture or ML/AI certifications, Kubernetes (CKA/CKAD), security/identity certifications, or enterprise architecture (TOGAF or equivalent).

We build robotic spacecraft that enable dynamic space operations, creating a future where maneuvering, upgrading, refueling, and exploration are as routine as they are on Earth. By developing the foundational capabilities that make sustained, responsive operations possible, we enable a new era of space activity that strengthens national security and ensures freedom of action in an increasingly contested domain.

Katalyst Culture

Working at Katalyst is intense, hands-on, and deeply rewarding. You’ll take real ownership and see your work move from concept to operations in an environment where the problems are hard and the impact is real. We value humility, craftsmanship, and doing things the right way, even when it’s harder. You’ll work closely with thoughtful, driven teammates who push each other to do their best.

What You’ll Do

Establish the technical baseline for Katalyst’s robotic spacecraft.
Translate work completed into a defined, repeatable system architecture.
Identify, define, and formalize interface and integration assumptions across subsystems.
Inject technical rigor into spacecraft development.
Raise and maintain the bar on systems-level thinking and decision-making without slowing execution.
Act as a system-level reviewer, ensuring architectural coherence and disciplined technical tradeoffs.
Build systems and structures for Katalyst's GEO program, establishing:
A clear requirements hierarchy with end-to-end traceability.
System-level diagrams and architectures that align teams around a shared technical vision.
Configuration and interface management practices that enable scale and repeatability.
Leadership
Take over management of functional-level engineering managers for current and future Katalyst missions
Provide consistent, credible technical leadership across the engineering organization.
Bring clarity, sound judgment, and calm to ambiguous, high-pressure situations.
Set clear expectations for engineering rigor, precision, and accountability in execution.

What We’re Looking For

Hands-on technical leadership with the ability to engage deeply in system-level decisions.
Comfort operating in ambiguity while holding exceptionally high standards for technical excellence.
Highly analytical, systems-oriented thinker capable of evaluating cross-functional trades and defining the appropriate level of clarity in analysis, documentation, and interfaces.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to create durable structures that allow teams to operate efficiently.
Leadership maturity: shaping a culture of credibility, humility, and pride in work while projecting calm urgency.

Your Ideal Background

8+ years of spacecraft engineering experience, with at least 5 years owning system-level architecture.
Prior accountability for end-to-end spacecraft design, not limited to a single subsystem.
Direct ownership of at least one spacecraft mission through flight, including system integration, test, and launch support.
Experience navigating at least one transition from:
Early demonstration missions to follow-on missions.
New product development and R&D efforts into operationalized, repeatable execution.
Proven experience leading multiple engineering disciplines simultaneously.

: Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed.

Director, Enterprise AI Platform Engineering

BMO is building a dedicated AI Engineering function to deliver the platform capabilities that make enterprise AI safe, governed, and scalable across our business domains and regulatory regimes. We are seeking an experienced technical leader to own the core infrastructure that governs and enforces how AI runs at BMO
- the AI Gateway, Policy Engine, Identity Fabric, AI Registry, Guardrails Runtime, and AI Observability.

This is a build-and-run
leadership role. You will lead a team that designs, ships, and operates the control and orchestration infrastructure sitting between policy authoring and inline enforcement — the capabilities every AI workload at BMO consumes to be secure, compliant, and observable. You will not own the AI models or applications themselves (those are domain-owned); you own the governed platform they run on
, and the runtime evidence that proves they run within policy.

You are a hands-on technical leader who has built platform capabilities at scale, operates what you build, and designs for operability and regulatory defensibility from day one. You blend deep engineering credibility with the executive presence to partner across Security, Architecture, DevOps, and domain teams. You are energized by taking real engineering assets — an existing developer portal, AI registry, a body of policy-as-code, and gateway integrations — and formalizing, scaling, and governing them into an enterprise-grade platform.

What You'll Own

Enterprise Control Plane

Developer Portal & AI Registry - productionize the developer portal; deliver a federated AI Registry spanning agents, models, tools, channels, and evaluations, with self-service onboarding and lifecycle workflows.
Policy Engine - policy-as-code infrastructure (Cedar/OPA), a policy compilation and GitOps distribution pipeline, risk-tiered approval workflows, and a policy simulation environment.
Observability & Audit - a multi-pipeline architecture spanning operational, security, and compliance telemetry; OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions; cross-pipeline trace correlation; and a tamper-evident audit lake producing regulator-ready evidence.
Governance & Lifecycle - certification workflows, automated compliance scoring, decommission governance, and evidence generation for architecture and model-risk review.

Domain Orchestration

Gateway Runtime - domain-hub deployment across multiple clouds; an inline enforcement engine with request-time policy evaluation, routing, residency, budget/quota controls, and circuit breakers, operating within strict latency budgets.
Guardrails Runtime - a multi-stage safety pipeline (input moderation, prompt-injection defense, PII handling, output validation, hallucination detection, policy enforcement) with bilingual (EN/FR) parity and behavioral guardrails for agentic workloads.
Identity Fabric - workload identity for AI (SPIFFE/SPIRE), token-exchange bridging, per-domain trust boundaries, enterprise identity integration, and cross-cloud token federation with zero-trust attestation.

What You'll Deliver (First 12 Months)

A production-hardened Developer Portal and federated AI Registry with sub-5-day self-service onboarding.
An AI Gateway operational in a selected business domain, meeting tiered latency targets.
Policy-as-code infrastructure distributing domain-scoped policy bundles via GitOps, with a working simulation sandbox.
A runtime evidence pipeline producing lineage-stamped, audit-ready traces aligned to model-risk and regulatory expectations.
A team scaled from an initial core (8–12 FTE) toward steady-state through a blend of net-new hiring and reallocation of experienced internal engineers.

How You'll Work

Build-run integrated - your team operates what it builds; there is no separate run team. You design for operability and Engineering support from the start.
Federated - you own the enforcement infrastructure domains consume; domains own their workloads. You enable, you don't centralize execution.
Evidence-first - regulatory evidence (e.g., OSFI E-23, OCC model-risk expectations) is produced at runtime through instrumented infrastructure, not assembled retroactively.
Capability-aligned - your teams own outcomes ("Identity Fabric works across all platforms"), not specific technologies.

Required Core Skills

Organizational & People Leadership

8+ years in technical platform, infrastructure, or AI/ML engineering roles in a large enterprise, including 4+ years leading and managing engineering teams.
Proven organizational leadership: building and scaling engineering teams from a small core to steady-state, including workforce planning, hiring, succession planning, and structuring squads for clear ownership and accountability.
Demonstrated team building across blended teams — integrating net-new hires with reallocated and seconded internal engineers into a single high-performing team with shared identity and standards.
Strong mentoring and coaching track record: developing engineers and technical leads, growing depth and bench strength, giving effective performance feedback, and creating clear technical growth pathways.
Ability to establish and sustain a healthy, inclusive team culture that promotes psychological safety, mutual respect, recognition, and employee engagement, aligned to BMO Values.
Experience leading through change and ambiguity — standing up a new function, aligning a team to a fast-evolving mandate, and maintaining momentum under tight timelines.
Conflict resolution and cross-team influence, including partnering with peer Directors on shared roadmaps and resolving competing priorities.

Platform & AI Engineering Depth

Demonstrated experience building and operating platform capabilities at scale — API gateways, policy/authorization systems, identity/workload-identity infrastructure, observability pipelines, or equivalent shared services.
Strong knowledge of GenAI platform engineering: LLM/AI gateways, model routing and abstraction, RAG and agentic patterns, guardrails, and AI evaluation approaches.
Hands-on experience with policy-as-code and authorization systems (Cedar, OPA/Rego, or equivalent) and GitOps-based distribution.
Experience with workload identity and zero-trust patterns (SPIFFE/SPIRE, mTLS, token exchange, federated identity) — or strong adjacent identity/security engineering depth.
Strong observability engineering background: OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, and telemetry pipelines across operational, security, and compliance domains.
Multi-cloud fluency (AWS and Azure preferred), cloud-native architecture, containerization/Kubernetes, and Infrastructure as Code.
Hands-on familiarity with modern AI/ML tooling (e.g., Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, SageMaker, Databricks, MLflow, LangChain, or equivalents) sufficient to lead technical direction.
Proven CI/CD, DevSecOps, and MLOps/LLMOps delivery experience.

Governance, Strategy & Communication

Solid grounding in Responsible AI, AI/data governance, privacy, and — ideally — model-risk management and financial-services regulatory expectations.
Executive-grade communication and relationship management across technical and senior-leadership audiences (written, verbal, and presentation).
Strategic and organizational management skills, including multi-year roadmap planning, budgeting, forecasting, and vendor engagement in partnership with Vendor Management.
A critical thinker with strong analytical, problem-solving, and prioritization abilities across a complex, multi-stakeholder portfolio.

Education & Certifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline (Master's preferred).
Relevant certifications an asset: cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) architecture or ML/AI certifications, Kubernetes (CKA/CKAD), security/identity certifications, or enterprise architecture (TOGAF or equivalent).

Group Director of Engineering

Full-time, Exempt

The Ocean House Collection (Company) includes three luxury properties on the Rhode Island shoreline.

Ocean House
(OH) is the Collection’s Forbes Five-Star flagship, offering 49 guest rooms, 20 signature suites, and 13 private villa vacation homes. Weekapaug Inn

Watch Hill Inn
, founded in 1845, combines historical charm with cutting-edge technology across 21 suite-style accommodations. Guests enjoy access to the full range of amenities, dining, and experiences at both Ocean House and Weekapaug Inn.

Scope of Position

The Group Director of Engineering oversees all Company maintenance operations including equipment maintenance and repair, landscaping, and residence maintenance, as well as monitoring ongoing preventative maintenance programs for all building management systems for all Company properties.

This encompasses, but is not limited to, physical building structure, all mechanical, electrical, H.V.A.C. systems and related equipment in accordance with energy conservation and preventative maintenance programs while ensuring the upkeep of guest areas to maintain an attractive hotel. The Group Director of Engineering will also manage all rehabilitation, expansion, and/or special capital improvements and capital maintenance projects, and other managed Company properties that may be known or unknown at this time including but not limited to: Ocean House, Weekapaug Inn, Watch Hill Inn, the Cottage Collection, the 20 Bay Street project, and all staff housing and offsite facilities whether owned or leased.

KNOWN CAPITAL PROJECTS

Redesign, permit and install Ocean House’s Septic System (System A and System B)
Manage construction and rebuild service road to the Beach per Coastal Resource Management Council (CRMC) approved plan
Manage construction of access road to redesigned OWTS (on site wastewater treatment system)
Manage construction of new beach storage area and associated access road
Manage redesign and re-construction of OH Beach Services Program to comply with CRMC Regulations
Design, permit and construct “temporary” decking around Dune Cottage

Position Summary

The Engineering Director provides strategic and hands-on technical leadership across all engineering functions at Ladish Valves. This role owns the full lifecycle of valve design and development — from initial customer specification through prototype fabrication, performance testing, regulatory compliance, and production release. The Engineering Director serves as the company's foremost technical authority on valve design, materials science, alloy selection, surface finishing, and precision lapping, ensuring that every product shipped meets or exceeds customer performance requirements and industry standards.
This is a high-visibility leadership position that partners closely with Sales, Manufacturing, Quality Assurance, and executive management to translate complex customer requirements into manufacturable, competitive valve solutions.
Valve Design & Engineering

Lead the end-to-end design of industrial valves including gate, globe, ball, check, butterfly, and specialty valves across pressure classes ANSI 150 through 4500.
Develop and maintain design standards, engineering calculations, and tolerance specifications for all valve families.
Direct the use of CAD/CAE tools (SolidWorks, AutoCAD, FEA) to produce detailed 3-D models, assembly drawings, and manufacturing packages.
Establish and enforce design-for-manufacturability (DFM) and design-for-testability (DFT) principles throughout the engineering team.
Oversee engineering change management, ensuring all design revisions are controlled, documented, and communicated to affected departments.
Research and integrate emerging design methodologies, seal technologies, and actuation systems to keep Ladish Valves at the competitive forefront.

Customization & Application Engineering

Act as the primary technical interface with customers requiring non-standard or highly engineered valve configurations.
Translate customer P&IDs, datasheets, purchase specifications, and operational parameters into fully engineered valve designs.
Provide detailed technical proposals, engineering data books, and application analyses in support of Sales during the quote and contract phase.
Lead technical review meetings (TQMs, kick-off meetings, and ITP reviews) with customers, third-party inspection agencies, and end users.
Manage engineering deliverables on engineered-to-order (ETO) and major project contracts, ensuring schedule and technical compliance.

Own the design, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the Ladish Valves test lab, including hydrostatic, pneumatic, cryogenic, fugitive emission, and functional test equipment.
Establish and enforce valve testing procedures in accordance with API 598, API 6D, , ASME B16.34, and customer-specific test specifications.
Direct root-cause analysis and corrective action for field failures, test rejections, and non-conformances, driving permanent engineering solutions.

Establish performance benchmarking programs to compare Ladish Valves products against competitive offerings.

Director, Enterprise AI Platform Engineering

BMO is building a dedicated AI Engineering function to deliver the platform capabilities that make enterprise AI safe, governed, and scalable across our business domains and regulatory regimes. We are seeking an experienced technical leader to own the core infrastructure that governs and enforces how AI runs at BMO
- the AI Gateway, Policy Engine, Identity Fabric, AI Registry, Guardrails Runtime, and AI Observability.

This is a build-and-run
leadership role. You will lead a team that designs, ships, and operates the control and orchestration infrastructure sitting between policy authoring and inline enforcement — the capabilities every AI workload at BMO consumes to be secure, compliant, and observable. You will not own the AI models or applications themselves (those are domain-owned); you own the governed platform they run on
, and the runtime evidence that proves they run within policy.

You are a hands-on technical leader who has built platform capabilities at scale, operates what you build, and designs for operability and regulatory defensibility from day one. You blend deep engineering credibility with the executive presence to partner across Security, Architecture, DevOps, and domain teams. You are energized by taking real engineering assets — an existing developer portal, AI registry, a body of policy-as-code, and gateway integrations — and formalizing, scaling, and governing them into an enterprise-grade platform.

What You'll Own

Enterprise Control Plane

Developer Portal & AI Registry - productionize the developer portal; deliver a federated AI Registry spanning agents, models, tools, channels, and evaluations, with self-service onboarding and lifecycle workflows.
Policy Engine - policy-as-code infrastructure (Cedar/OPA), a policy compilation and GitOps distribution pipeline, risk-tiered approval workflows, and a policy simulation environment.
Observability & Audit - a multi-pipeline architecture spanning operational, security, and compliance telemetry; OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions; cross-pipeline trace correlation; and a tamper-evident audit lake producing regulator-ready evidence.
Governance & Lifecycle - certification workflows, automated compliance scoring, decommission governance, and evidence generation for architecture and model-risk review.

Domain Orchestration

Gateway Runtime - domain-hub deployment across multiple clouds; an inline enforcement engine with request-time policy evaluation, routing, residency, budget/quota controls, and circuit breakers, operating within strict latency budgets.
Guardrails Runtime - a multi-stage safety pipeline (input moderation, prompt-injection defense, PII handling, output validation, hallucination detection, policy enforcement) with bilingual (EN/FR) parity and behavioral guardrails for agentic workloads.
Identity Fabric - workload identity for AI (SPIFFE/SPIRE), token-exchange bridging, per-domain trust boundaries, enterprise identity integration, and cross-cloud token federation with zero-trust attestation.

What You'll Deliver (First 12 Months)

A production-hardened Developer Portal and federated AI Registry with sub-5-day self-service onboarding.
An AI Gateway operational in a selected business domain, meeting tiered latency targets.
Policy-as-code infrastructure distributing domain-scoped policy bundles via GitOps, with a working simulation sandbox.
A runtime evidence pipeline producing lineage-stamped, audit-ready traces aligned to model-risk and regulatory expectations.
A team scaled from an initial core (8–12 FTE) toward steady-state through a blend of net-new hiring and reallocation of experienced internal engineers.

How You'll Work

Build-run integrated - your team operates what it builds; there is no separate run team. You design for operability and Engineering support from the start.
Federated - you own the enforcement infrastructure domains consume; domains own their workloads. You enable, you don't centralize execution.
Evidence-first - regulatory evidence (e.g., OSFI E-23, OCC model-risk expectations) is produced at runtime through instrumented infrastructure, not assembled retroactively.
Capability-aligned - your teams own outcomes ("Identity Fabric works across all platforms"), not specific technologies.

Organizational & People Leadership

8+ years in technical platform, infrastructure, or AI/ML engineering roles in a large enterprise, including 4+ years leading and managing engineering teams.
Proven organizational leadership: building and scaling engineering teams from a small core to steady-state, including workforce planning, hiring, succession planning, and structuring squads for clear ownership and accountability.
Demonstrated team building across blended teams — integrating net-new hires with reallocated and seconded internal engineers into a single high-performing team with shared identity and standards.
Strong mentoring and coaching track record: developing engineers and technical leads, growing depth and bench strength, giving effective performance feedback, and creating clear technical growth pathways.
Ability to establish and sustain a healthy, inclusive team culture that promotes psychological safety, mutual respect, recognition, and employee engagement, aligned to BMO Values.
Experience leading through change and ambiguity — standing up a new function, aligning a team to a fast-evolving mandate, and maintaining momentum under tight timelines.
Conflict resolution and cross-team influence, including partnering with peer Directors on shared roadmaps and resolving competing priorities.

Platform & AI Engineering Depth

Demonstrated experience building and operating platform capabilities at scale — API gateways, policy/authorization systems, identity/workload-identity infrastructure, observability pipelines, or equivalent shared services.
Strong knowledge of GenAI platform engineering: LLM/AI gateways, model routing and abstraction, RAG and agentic patterns, guardrails, and AI evaluation approaches.
Hands-on experience with policy-as-code and authorization systems (Cedar, OPA/Rego, or equivalent) and GitOps-based distribution.
Experience with workload identity and zero-trust patterns (SPIFFE/SPIRE, mTLS, token exchange, federated identity) — or strong adjacent identity/security engineering depth.
Strong observability engineering background: OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, and telemetry pipelines across operational, security, and compliance domains.
Multi-cloud fluency (AWS and Azure preferred), cloud-native architecture, containerization/Kubernetes, and Infrastructure as Code.
Hands-on familiarity with modern AI/ML tooling (e.g., Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, SageMaker, Databricks, MLflow, LangChain, or equivalents) sufficient to lead technical direction.
Proven CI/CD, DevSecOps, and MLOps/LLMOps delivery experience.

Solid grounding in Responsible AI, AI/data governance, privacy, and — ideally — model-risk management and financial-services regulatory expectations.
Executive-grade communication and relationship management across technical and senior-leadership audiences (written, verbal, and presentation).
Strategic and organizational management skills, including multi-year roadmap planning, budgeting, forecasting, and vendor engagement in partnership with Vendor Management.
A critical thinker with strong analytical, problem-solving, and prioritization abilities across a complex, multi-stakeholder portfolio.

Relevant certifications an asset: cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) architecture or ML/AI certifications, Kubernetes (CKA/CKAD), security/identity certifications, or enterprise architecture (TOGAF or equivalent).

Translate work completed into a defined, repeatable system architecture.
Identify, define, and formalize interface and integration assumptions across subsystems.
Inject technical rigor into spacecraft development.
Raise and maintain the bar on systems-level thinking and decision-making without slowing execution.
Act as a system-level reviewer, ensuring architectural coherence and disciplined technical tradeoffs.
Build systems and structures for Katalyst's GEO program, establishing:
A clear requirements hierarchy with end-to-end traceability.
System-level diagrams and architectures that align teams around a shared technical vision.
Configuration and interface management practices that enable scale and repeatability.
Leadership
Take over management of functional-level engineering managers for current and future Katalyst missions
Provide consistent, credible technical leadership across the engineering organization.
Bring clarity, sound judgment, and calm to ambiguous, high-pressure situations.
Set clear expectations for engineering rigor, precision, and accountability in execution.

Hands-on technical leadership with the ability to engage deeply in system-level decisions.
Comfort operating in ambiguity while holding exceptionally high standards for technical excellence.
Highly analytical, systems-oriented thinker capable of evaluating cross-functional trades and defining the appropriate level of clarity in analysis, documentation, and interfaces.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to create durable structures that allow teams to operate efficiently.
Leadership maturity: shaping a culture of credibility, humility, and pride in work while projecting calm urgency.

Direct ownership of at least one spacecraft mission through flight, including system integration, test, and launch support.

Director, Enterprise AI Platform Engineering

BMO is building a dedicated AI Engineering function to deliver the platform capabilities that make enterprise AI safe, governed, and scalable across our business domains and regulatory regimes. We are seeking an experienced technical leader to own the core infrastructure that governs and enforces how AI runs at BMO
- the AI Gateway, Policy Engine, Identity Fabric, AI Registry, Guardrails Runtime, and AI Observability.

This is a build-and-run
leadership role. You will lead a team that designs, ships, and operates the control and orchestration infrastructure sitting between policy authoring and inline enforcement — the capabilities every AI workload at BMO consumes to be secure, compliant, and observable. You will not own the AI models or applications themselves (those are domain-owned); you own the governed platform they run on
, and the runtime evidence that proves they run within policy.

You are a hands-on technical leader who has built platform capabilities at scale, operates what you build, and designs for operability and regulatory defensibility from day one. You blend deep engineering credibility with the executive presence to partner across Security, Architecture, DevOps, and domain teams. You are energized by taking real engineering assets — an existing developer portal, AI registry, a body of policy-as-code, and gateway integrations — and formalizing, scaling, and governing them into an enterprise-grade platform.

What You'll Own

Enterprise Control Plane

Developer Portal & AI Registry - productionize the developer portal; deliver a federated AI Registry spanning agents, models, tools, channels, and evaluations, with self-service onboarding and lifecycle workflows.
Policy Engine - policy-as-code infrastructure (Cedar/OPA), a policy compilation and GitOps distribution pipeline, risk-tiered approval workflows, and a policy simulation environment.
Observability & Audit - a multi-pipeline architecture spanning operational, security, and compliance telemetry; OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions; cross-pipeline trace correlation; and a tamper-evident audit lake producing regulator-ready evidence.
Governance & Lifecycle - certification workflows, automated compliance scoring, decommission governance, and evidence generation for architecture and model-risk review.

Domain Orchestration

Gateway Runtime - domain-hub deployment across multiple clouds; an inline enforcement engine with request-time policy evaluation, routing, residency, budget/quota controls, and circuit breakers, operating within strict latency budgets.
Guardrails Runtime - a multi-stage safety pipeline (input moderation, prompt-injection defense, PII handling, output validation, hallucination detection, policy enforcement) with bilingual (EN/FR) parity and behavioral guardrails for agentic workloads.
Identity Fabric - workload identity for AI (SPIFFE/SPIRE), token-exchange bridging, per-domain trust boundaries, enterprise identity integration, and cross-cloud token federation with zero-trust attestation.

What You'll Deliver (First 12 Months)

A production-hardened Developer Portal and federated AI Registry with sub-5-day self-service onboarding.
An AI Gateway operational in a selected business domain, meeting tiered latency targets.
Policy-as-code infrastructure distributing domain-scoped policy bundles via GitOps, with a working simulation sandbox.
A runtime evidence pipeline producing lineage-stamped, audit-ready traces aligned to model-risk and regulatory expectations.
A team scaled from an initial core (8–12 FTE) toward steady-state through a blend of net-new hiring and reallocation of experienced internal engineers.

How You'll Work

Build-run integrated - your team operates what it builds; there is no separate run team. You design for operability and Engineering support from the start.
Federated - you own the enforcement infrastructure domains consume; domains own their workloads. You enable, you don't centralize execution.
Evidence-first - regulatory evidence (e.g., OSFI E-23, OCC model-risk expectations) is produced at runtime through instrumented infrastructure, not assembled retroactively.
Capability-aligned - your teams own outcomes ("Identity Fabric works across all platforms"), not specific technologies.

Required Core Skills

Organizational & People Leadership

8+ years in technical platform, infrastructure, or AI/ML engineering roles in a large enterprise, including 4+ years leading and managing engineering teams.
Proven organizational leadership: building and scaling engineering teams from a small core to steady-state, including workforce planning, hiring, succession planning, and structuring squads for clear ownership and accountability.
Demonstrated team building across blended teams — integrating net-new hires with reallocated and seconded internal engineers into a single high-performing team with shared identity and standards.
Strong mentoring and coaching track record: developing engineers and technical leads, growing depth and bench strength, giving effective performance feedback, and creating clear technical growth pathways.
Ability to establish and sustain a healthy, inclusive team culture that promotes psychological safety, mutual respect, recognition, and employee engagement, aligned to BMO Values.
Experience leading through change and ambiguity — standing up a new function, aligning a team to a fast-evolving mandate, and maintaining momentum under tight timelines.
Conflict resolution and cross-team influence, including partnering with peer Directors on shared roadmaps and resolving competing priorities.

Platform & AI Engineering Depth

Demonstrated experience building and operating platform capabilities at scale — API gateways, policy/authorization systems, identity/workload-identity infrastructure, observability pipelines, or equivalent shared services.
Strong knowledge of GenAI platform engineering: LLM/AI gateways, model routing and abstraction, RAG and agentic patterns, guardrails, and AI evaluation approaches.
Hands-on experience with policy-as-code and authorization systems (Cedar, OPA/Rego, or equivalent) and GitOps-based distribution.
Experience with workload identity and zero-trust patterns (SPIFFE/SPIRE, mTLS, token exchange, federated identity) — or strong adjacent identity/security engineering depth.
Strong observability engineering background: OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, and telemetry pipelines across operational, security, and compliance domains.
Multi-cloud fluency (AWS and Azure preferred), cloud-native architecture, containerization/Kubernetes, and Infrastructure as Code.
Hands-on familiarity with modern AI/ML tooling (e.g., Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, SageMaker, Databricks, MLflow, LangChain, or equivalents) sufficient to lead technical direction.
Proven CI/CD, DevSecOps, and MLOps/LLMOps delivery experience.

Governance, Strategy & Communication

Solid grounding in Responsible AI, AI/data governance, privacy, and — ideally — model-risk management and financial-services regulatory expectations.
Executive-grade communication and relationship management across technical and senior-leadership audiences (written, verbal, and presentation).
Strategic and organizational management skills, including multi-year roadmap planning, budgeting, forecasting, and vendor engagement in partnership with Vendor Management.
A critical thinker with strong analytical, problem-solving, and prioritization abilities across a complex, multi-stakeholder portfolio.

Education & Certifications

Relevant certifications an asset: cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) architecture or ML/AI certifications, Kubernetes (CKA/CKAD), security/identity certifications, or enterprise architecture (TOGAF or equivalent).

- the AI Gateway, Policy Engine, Identity Fabric, AI Registry, Guardrails Runtime, and AI Observability.

leadership role. You will lead a team that designs, ships, and operates the control and orchestration infrastructure sitting between policy authoring and inline enforcement — the capabilities every AI workload at BMO consumes to be secure, compliant, and observable. You will not own the AI models or applications themselves (those are domain-owned); you own the governed platform they run on
, and the runtime evidence that proves they run within policy.

You are a hands-on technical leader who has built platform capabilities at scale, operates what you build, and designs for operability and regulatory defensibility from day one. You blend deep engineering credibility with the executive presence to partner across Security, Architecture, DevOps, and domain teams. You are energized by taking real engineering assets — an existing developer portal, AI registry, a body of policy-as-code, and gateway integrations — and formalizing, scaling, and governing them into an enterprise-grade platform.

What You'll Own

Enterprise Control Plane

Developer Portal & AI Registry - productionize the developer portal; deliver a federated AI Registry spanning agents, models, tools, channels, and evaluations, with self-service onboarding and lifecycle workflows.
Policy Engine - policy-as-code infrastructure (Cedar/OPA), a policy compilation and GitOps distribution pipeline, risk-tiered approval workflows, and a policy simulation environment.
Observability & Audit - a multi-pipeline architecture spanning operational, security, and compliance telemetry; OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions; cross-pipeline trace correlation; and a tamper-evident audit lake producing regulator-ready evidence.
Governance & Lifecycle - certification workflows, automated compliance scoring, decommission governance, and evidence generation for architecture and model-risk review.

Domain Orchestration

Gateway Runtime - domain-hub deployment across multiple clouds; an inline enforcement engine with request-time policy evaluation, routing, residency, budget/quota controls, and circuit breakers, operating within strict latency budgets.
Guardrails Runtime - a multi-stage safety pipeline (input moderation, prompt-injection defense, PII handling, output validation, hallucination detection, policy enforcement) with bilingual (EN/FR) parity and behavioral guardrails for agentic workloads.
Identity Fabric - workload identity for AI (SPIFFE/SPIRE), token-exchange bridging, per-domain trust boundaries, enterprise identity integration, and cross-cloud token federation with zero-trust attestation.

What You'll Deliver (First 12 Months)

A production-hardened Developer Portal and federated AI Registry with sub-5-day self-service onboarding.
An AI Gateway operational in a selected business domain, meeting tiered latency targets.
Policy-as-code infrastructure distributing domain-scoped policy bundles via GitOps, with a working simulation sandbox.
A runtime evidence pipeline producing lineage-stamped, audit-ready traces aligned to model-risk and regulatory expectations.
A team scaled from an initial core (8–12 FTE) toward steady-state through a blend of net-new hiring and reallocation of experienced internal engineers.

How You'll Work

Build-run integrated - your team operates what it builds; there is no separate run team. You design for operability and Engineering support from the start.
Federated - you own the enforcement infrastructure domains consume; domains own their workloads. You enable, you don't centralize execution.
Evidence-first - regulatory evidence (e.g., OSFI E-23, OCC model-risk expectations) is produced at runtime through instrumented infrastructure, not assembled retroactively.
Capability-aligned - your teams own outcomes ("Identity Fabric works across all platforms"), not specific technologies.

Required Core Skills

Organizational & People Leadership

Proven organizational leadership: building and scaling engineering teams from a small core to steady-state, including workforce planning, hiring, succession planning, and structuring squads for clear ownership and accountability.

Strong mentoring and coaching track record: developing engineers and technical leads, growing depth and bench strength, giving effective performance feedback, and creating clear technical growth pathways.
Ability to establish and sustain a healthy, inclusive team culture that promotes psychological safety, mutual respect, recognition, and employee engagement, aligned to BMO Values.
Experience leading through change and ambiguity — standing up a new function, aligning a team to a fast-evolving mandate, and maintaining momentum under tight timelines.
Conflict resolution and cross-team influence, including partnering with peer Directors on shared roadmaps and resolving competing priorities.

Platform & AI Engineering Depth

Observability & Audit - a multi-pipeline architecture spanning operational, security, and compliance telemetry; OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions; cross-pipeline trace correlation; and a tamper-evident audit lake producing regulator-ready evidence.

Guardrails Runtime - a multi-stage safety pipeline (input moderation, prompt-injection defense, PII handling, output validation, hallucination detection, policy enforcement) with bilingual (EN/FR) parity and behavioral guardrails for agentic workloads.
Identity Fabric - workload identity for AI (SPIFFE/SPIRE), token-exchange bridging, per-domain trust boundaries, enterprise identity integration, and cross-cloud token federation with zero-trust attestation.
